newsitem.title: USA: N.J. computer plan would cost $2.5 bln -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. computer plan would cost $2.5 bln -- paper.

text.p: A plan to upgrade computer access for New Jersey public schools would cost $2.5 billion over five years, the Bergen Record reported Tuesday.
The plan envisions giving all schools internet access, and improving the ratio of computers to pupils.
State Ratepayer Advocate Blossom Peretz proposed the idea, and said it could be financed in part from fees on telecommunications companies, taxes on video rentals, and special bond sales.
The Board of Public Utilities is set to vote September 15 on an initial financing plan for the proposal.
